body:
Confirmed in 4.5.1.stable.mono as well.

### System information
macOS M4 Max, Tahoe 4.6.1, OpenGL 3 Forward+

### Steps to Reproduce
Cannot reliably reproduce; it is an intermittent error. But very similar to the original description.

In my case, I am preloading `StyleBoxTexture` resource files early in the main scene's `_Ready` method for performance, & caching them in a C# Dictionary in an autoload class to avoid garbage collection. Various scenes throughout the game's lifecycle are then instantiated & freed, which already contain hardcoded references to these same StyleBoxTexture resource files, set in the editor.

I am not sure if there is a better approach to work around this error, but it definitely eliminated noticeable loading delays for large textures (4K to 5K resolution), at least on an older machine.

I should probably mention that I'm performing the same procedure for a custom `Theme` resource file because it takes significantly longer than the style resources to load, even on an M4 Max. I'm leaning toward the textures as the root cause, rather than the theme, based on the original description - haven't tested this idea due to the intermittent nature of the error.

### Stack Trace
```
E 0:02:57:074   void System.ThrowHelper.ThrowInvalidOperationException_HandleIsNotInitialized(): System.InvalidOperationException: Handle is not initialized.

                ScriptManagerBridge.cs:1280 @ Godot.NativeInterop.godot_bool Godot.Bridge.ScriptManagerBridge.SwapGCHandleForType(nint, System.IntPtr*, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_bool)
```

### Related Issues
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/100691 (I make heavy use of tweens, but since this was fixed in 4.5, I don't think it is the cause.)

I'm on windows 11, it was reported to me form steamdeck (so a flavour of linux) too.

I'm on 4.5.1 and this also keeps happing to me, I released a game build on Steam and the users have been reporting this to me too, unfortunately on some systems like a steamdeck this causes crashes too.
It happens when I switch scenes, stacktrace in my code leads to my just calling Load (Godot method) to load a scene and then it does this. I have two main scenes which I load and remove and it happens with both of them.
(I think this might be some issue with handling resources, not just textures perhaps?)

I think considering the above and mine here, this could be considered confirmed perhaps or is there something extra for that needed?

This is also happening to me when loading custom resources from a pre-loaded pool in C#:

@AThousandShips Sorry for the ping but I've been encountering this fairly consistently on a Godot 4.7.2 Mono game, with the same SwapGCHandleForType / Handle is not initialized stack trace.

What's worse, users are reporting crashes due to this, on (at least) these configs:
D3D12 12_0 - Forward Mobile - Using Device #0: NVIDIA - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 6GB
D3D12 12_0 - Forward Mobile - Using Device #0: NVIDIA - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU

These crashes are blocking me from participating in Steam Nextfest and then I noticed the recent work addressing the GCHandle race by @AdmiralFrijoles above and was filled with a sudden gust of hope :)

EDIT:
Moving to IgnoreDeep while loading the resources seem to have fixed the "Handle is not initialized" crashes:
var resource = ResourceLoader.Load(resourcePath, typeHint, ResourceLoader.CacheMode.IgnoreDeep);

But users still reports crashes with this log:
Godot Engine v4.7.2.stable.mono.official.ed1daf0bf - https://godotengine.org/
D3D12 12_0 - Forward Mobile - Using Device #0: NVIDIA - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 Ti

ERROR: FATAL: Index p_index = 2 is out of bounds (size() = 0).
at: get (./core/templates/cowdata.h:197)
C# backtrace (most recent call first):
[0] Godot.Node Godot.PackedScene.Instantiate(Godot.PackedScene+GenEditState)
Noted, this is already tracked by the relevant team so there's nothing I can add here for now

Cross-referencing a related report I just filed: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/124498

It reproduces this same `SwapGCHandleForType` -> `GCHandle.FromIntPtr` failure branch (`CSharpInstance::refcount_incremented()` clears `gchandle.handle` before the swap and returns on failure without clearing `inited`/the weak type), and adds two entry points that hit the same cleared handle:

- the binding-free path: `_instance_binding_free_callback()` -> `SetGodotObjectPtr(script_binding.gchandle.get_intptr(), nullptr)`
- a process abort: `ERROR: FATAL: Condition "gchandle.get_intptr().value != p_old_gchandle.value" is true` -> `handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 4` in `godotsharp_internal_unmanaged_instance_binding_create_managed()` (that line carries a `// TODO: Possible data race?`).

Fresh numbers from a C# stress probe (Godot 4.7.2.stable.mono, headless, 32 load/instantiate/free cycles in one process, no forced GC): 13 runs -> 4 runs emitted `Handle is not initialized` (1, 1, 9 and 1 occurrences; once a binding is cleared the error repeats on every later refcount increase of that same object, 9x inside a single cycle in one run), and 1 run aborted with the FATAL condition above.
